introduction.name: J Raghavendra
introduction.title: Distributed Systems & Cloud Infrastructure Engineer
introduction.summary: Computer Science student specializing in distributed consensus, concurrency primitives, and systems-level network programming. Experienced in building zero-copy stream decoders and high-throughput backend services capable of predictable P99 latency under heavy load.

story: I started my engineering journey by taking apart open-source network daemons to understand what actually happens when a packet hits a network card. That curiosity quickly evolved into a deep dedication to distributed systems, low-level concurrency, and infrastructure efficiency.

As a software engineering student, I don't just write code that passes happy-path tests; I obsess over what happens when a node fails, when network partitions delay packets, and when CPU cache invalidations derail P99 latency.

In my past internships at Apex Cloud Technologies and Novaflow Systems, I worked alongside staff engineers to build mission-critical caching and telemetry services handling millions of daily operations. I thrive in teams that value strong design docs, rigorous code reviews, and high engineering standards.

philosophy.title: Measure Before Optimizing
philosophy.desc: Never guess bottlenecks. Always collect CPU flamegraphs, memory allocation profiles, and P99 percentiles before writing custom fast-paths. Deconstruct ambiguous problems into formal invariants and boundary conditions.

philosophy.title: Memory Safety & Deterministic Concurrency
philosophy.desc: Leverage strict type systems, immutability, and explicit error handling. Avoid shared mutable state in favor of message passing and lock-striped partitioning to eliminate race conditions by design.

philosophy.title: First-Principles Source Code Investigation
philosophy.desc: Read canonical RFC specifications, kernel docs, and battle-tested codebases (Redis, Linux, Raft, FoundationDB). Build concrete prototypes and stress-test them under simulated network chaos rather than relying solely on high-level abstractions.

philosophy.title: Clarity, Reliability & Observability First
philosophy.desc: The best engineering is maintainable, readable, and predictable. Eschew convoluted tricks in favor of sound architecture. Instrument every microservice with metrics and traces from day one so failure states are immediately actionable.

philosophy.title: Fail Fast, Recover Gracefully
philosophy.desc: Distributed networks will fail. Systems must be designed around defensive timeouts, exponential backoffs, circuit breakers, and deterministic consensus. Graceful degradation beats cascading failure every time.
